-        "over-commit. Operations return Result to make failure modes explicit."
+        "over-commit. Operations return Result to make failure modes explicit, and batch"
+        "operations commit atomically — all steps succeed, or none are applied."

+decision AtomicBatchesAsResultChain
+    date = "2026-04-16"
+    reason =
+        "A multi-line order, a truck delivery for many SKUs, or a fleet-wide rebalance must"
+        "either apply every operation or leave the inventory untouched. Because Inventory is"
+        "immutable, folding a list of operations through the existing checked single-step"
+        "functions already has that property: each step returns Result<Inventory, String>, and"
+        "a failure simply short-circuits the fold so the intermediate inventory is discarded"
+        "before any caller observes it. There is no separate transaction log, rollback step, or"
+        "two-phase commit — the Result chain is the atomicity mechanism. The batch error embeds"
+        "the zero-based index of the first failing operation so callers can pinpoint the cause."
+    chosen = "FoldOverCheckedSteps"
+    rejected = ["TransactionLogWithRollback", "BestEffortSkipFailures", "MutableStagingBuffer"]
+    impacts = [reserveBatch, receiveShipmentBatch, rebalanceBatch]

     id: String
     name: String

+fn annotateBatchError(opKind: String, index: Int, err: String) -> String
+    ? "Prefixes a batch step error with the operation kind and zero-based index."

+
+verify annotateBatchError

+fn seededInventory() -> Inventory
+    ? "Fixture used by batch verify blocks: W1 and W2 registered, S1 and S2 registered,"
+      "W1 holds 10 of S1 and 5 of S2, W2 holds 2 of S1 on hand."
+    inv0 = emptyInventory()
+    inv1 = registerWarehouse(inv0, Warehouse(id = "W1", location = "NYC"))
+    inv2 = registerWarehouse(inv1, Warehouse(id = "W2", location = "LA"))
+    inv3 = registerSku(inv2, Sku(id = "S1", name = "Widget", reorderPoint = 3))
+    inv4 = registerSku(inv3, Sku(id = "S2", name = "Gadget", reorderPoint = 1))
+    inv5 = applyReceive(inv4, "W1", "S1", 10)
+    inv6 = applyReceive(inv5, "W1", "S2", 5)
+    applyReceive(inv6, "W2", "S1", 2)
+
+verify seededInventory

+    availableStock(seededInventory(), "W1", "S2") => 5
+    availableStock(seededInventory(), "W2", "S1") => 2
+
+fn reserveBatchFrom(inv: Inventory, ops: List<ReserveOp>, index: Int) -> Result<Inventory, String>
+    ? "Folds reservations starting at 'index'. Returns the updated inventory on full success,"
+      "or the first failure annotated with the offending index."
+    match ops
+        [] -> Result.Ok(inv)
+        [op, ..rest] -> reserveBatchStep(inv, op, rest, index)
+

+# --- Atomic batch operations --------------------------------------------------
+#
+# A batch is a sequence of operation descriptors. ``apply_batch`` applies them
+# left-to-right on a local copy of the inventory; if any operation raises, the
+# caller's inventory remains untouched (since Inventory is immutable and the
+# working copy is never assigned back) and ``BatchError`` is raised identifying
+# the failing operation's index and payload.
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ShipmentOp:
+    warehouse_id: str
+    sku_id: str
+    qty: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ReserveOp:
+    warehouse_id: str
+    sku_id: str
+    qty: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ReleaseOp:
+    warehouse_id: str
+    sku_id: str
+    qty: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class FulfillOp:
+    warehouse_id: str
+    sku_id: str
+    qty: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class RebalanceOp:
+    from_id: str
+    to_id: str
+    sku_id: str
+    qty: int
+
+
+BatchOp = Union[ShipmentOp, ReserveOp, ReleaseOp, FulfillOp, RebalanceOp]
+
+
+class BatchError(ValueError):
+    """Raised when an operation inside ``apply_batch`` fails.
+
+    The inventory passed to ``apply_batch`` is left unchanged. ``index`` points at
+    the zero-based position of the failing operation; ``op`` is the descriptor;
+    ``cause`` is the underlying ValueError message.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, index: int, op: BatchOp, cause: BaseException) -> None:
+        self.index = index
+        self.op = op
+        self.cause = cause
+        super().__init__(
+            f"Batch operation {index} ({type(op).__name__}) failed: {cause}"
+        )
+
+
+def _apply_op(inv: Inventory, op: BatchOp) -> Inventory:
+    """Dispatch a single batch op to the matching single-step function."""
+    if isinstance(op, ShipmentOp):
+        return receive_shipment(inv, op.warehouse_id, op.sku_id, op.qty)
+    if isinstance(op, ReserveOp):
+        return reserve_stock(inv, op.warehouse_id, op.sku_id, op.qty)
+    if isinstance(op, ReleaseOp):
+        return release_reservation(inv, op.warehouse_id, op.sku_id, op.qty)
+    if isinstance(op, FulfillOp):
+        return fulfill_reservation(inv, op.warehouse_id, op.sku_id, op.qty)
+    if isinstance(op, RebalanceOp):
+        return rebalance(inv, op.from_id, op.to_id, op.sku_id, op.qty)
+    raise TypeError(f"Unknown batch op: {type(op).__name__}")
+
+
+def apply_batch(inv: Inventory, ops: list[BatchOp]) -> Inventory:
+    """Apply every op in ``ops`` atomically.
+
+    Returns a new Inventory reflecting all ops if every one succeeds. If any op
+    raises ValueError, ``apply_batch`` raises ``BatchError`` with the failing
+    index and op; the caller's ``inv`` is unchanged.
+    """
+    working = inv
+    for i, op in enumerate(ops):
+        try:
+            working = _apply_op(working, op)
+        except ValueError as exc:
+            raise BatchError(i, op, exc) from exc
+    return working
+

+    Returns a new event list reflecting every accepted item if all normalize
+    cleanly. If any item raises ``ValueError`` (bad provider, unknown kind,
+    etc.), the function raises ``BatchIngestError`` wrapping the failing index,
+    the original item, and the underlying cause; the ``events`` list the
+    caller passed in is not modified.

+    list and feed the resulting anomaly drafts through ``materializeNewCases``
+    just like before, so anomalies discovered inside a successfully applied
+    batch still open manual-review cases.

 Tasks move through Todo → InProgress → Done, with Blocked as an off-path state.
+Projects may be archived: an archived project is read-only and rejects any
+mutation (membership changes, new tasks, task state changes) until it is

+Design decisions:
+
+* Archival is a single Bool field on the Project record, not a new stage
+  in a project-state enum and not a separate archive record. Archival is
+  a binary lifecycle flag: a project is either active or archived, and
+  archiving/unarchiving is symmetric. A bool keeps the Project record a
+  single source of truth and lets permission predicates compose the check
+  into existing rules without a parallel type. Alternatives considered:
+  a Project state enum, a separate Archive record referencing the
+  project.

guess.intent: Add an atomic batch webhook ingestion method (apply_batch) to PaymentLedger that rolls back on failure via a new BatchError, with tests demonstrating all-or-nothing semantics.

+    Severity starts from a kind-specific base tier; large amounts then

+            "refund_missing_settlement",
+        }
+    )

+        {
+            "settlement_capture_mismatch",
+            "settlement_refund_mismatch",
+        }
+    )
+
+    # Amount thresholds in minor units (cents). A $1k mismatch bumps one
+    # tier; a $100k mismatch is Urgent regardless of base kind.
+    _LARGE_AMOUNT_CENTS: int = 10_000_000
+    _MEDIUM_AMOUNT_CENTS: int = 100_000

+        if kind in cls._HIGH_KINDS:
